claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. 

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

Do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have a child - Alex, who's 8 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand a bit more about your situation.

Are you living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about Alex's situation.

Is Alex under 16 years old, or if they're 16 or over, are they in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is only 8, so yes, under 16.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to ask about your responsibility for Alex.

Are you the person responsible for Alex? This generally means Alex lives with you and you're looking after them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. Alex lives with me and I look after them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment.

Is anyone else also claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure - I don't know if anyone else is claiming for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: That's okay. Let me ask this differently - does Alex live with anyone else, or do they only live with you?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Let me just check a couple more details to complete the assessment.

Do you have the right to reside in the UK? This means you're either a UK citizen, have settled status, or have the right to live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do have the right to reside in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. One final question:

Is Alex in hospital or in care (such as being looked after by the local authority)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in hospital or in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me and the UK Child Benefit eligibility rules, I can now provide you with an assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on your circumstances, you meet all the requirements:
- ✓ You live in the UK with the right to reside
- ✓ Alex is under 16 (aged 8)
- ✓ Alex lives with you and you're responsible for them
- ✓ Alex is not in hospital or care
- ✓ No one else is claiming for Alex

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. Please note that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, but you would still be eligible to claim.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
